skills.name: add-datasource
skills.description: Use for the implementation workflow that adds gcx CLI support for a datasource type not registered in internal/datasources/providers — query client, command constructors, DatasourceProvider registration. Trigger on "add support for an unsupported datasource type" or "new datasource type". NOT for creating or configuring a datasource instance in a Grafana stack, extending an already-registered kind, deciding the integration tier, or running pre-review self-checks.

skills.name: add-provider
skills.description: Use for the implementation workflow once a capability is already classified as a Grafana Cloud product provider such as SLO, OnCall, Synthetic Monitoring, k6, or ML — provider package, commands, config keys, and optional resource adapters. Trigger on "add provider", "new provider", or "build the product provider". NOT for deciding whether something should be a provider.

skills.name: council-mode
skills.description: Run a bounded supervisor-mediated advisor council. Use when the user asks for council mode, asks to convene advisors, debate a decision, cross-examine recommendations, or run /council.

skills.name: create-dashboard
skills.description: Designs and creates Grafana dashboards with gcx, using dashboard snapshots as a visual feedback loop. Use to create dashboards, add panels, variables, or annotations, design queries or layout, or make a material visual redesign. Trigger on create dashboard, new dashboard, build dashboard, add panels, add variable, or add annotation.

skills.name: debug-with-grafana
skills.description: Structured workflow for investigating application problems with Grafana observability data: metrics, logs, and traces. Covers live firefighting and retrospective incident analysis, triage, root cause, blast radius, rollout verification, errors, latency, retries, and queue backlogs.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask how to do something, find a skill, ask whether a skill can perform a task, or want to extend agent capabilities.

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and choices that do not read as templated defaults.

skills.name: gcx
skills.description: Manages Grafana Cloud resources via the gcx CLI. Trigger when the user wants to inspect, create, update, delete, query, or automate dashboards, datasources, alerts, SLOs, synthetic checks, oncall, incidents, fleet, k6, knowledge graph, or adaptive telemetry.

skills.name: mcp-scripting
skills.description: Write mcpScript JavaScript for discovering, inspecting, and calling MCP tools.

skills.name: pi-lens-ast-grep
skills.description: Use when searching or replacing code patterns. Use ast-grep instead of text search for semantic and structural accuracy.

skills.name: pi-lens-lsp-navigation
skills.description: Navigate code with IDE features and run proactive LSP diagnostics on files, folders, and batches. Use as primary code intelligence for definitions, references, types, and errors.

skills.name: pi-lens-write-ast-grep-rule
skills.description: Use when writing a new pi-lens ast-grep rule YAML file. Covers schema, drop path, gotchas, and NAPI runner constraints.

skills.name: pi-lens-write-tree-sitter-rule
skills.description: Use when writing a new pi-lens tree-sitter query rule YAML file. Covers schema, S-expression syntax, capture names, predicates, and gotchas.

skills.name: pi-subagents
skills.description: Delegate work to builtin or custom subagents with single-agent, parallel, scripted chaining, async, forked-context, and coordinated workflows. Use for advisory review, implementation handoffs, and multi-step tasks where one agent stays in control while others contribute.

skills.name: ponytail
skills.description: Forces the laziest solution that actually works: simplest, shortest, most minimal. Question whether the task needs to exist, use standard library before custom code, native features before dependencies, and one line before fifty. Use on ANY coding task: writing, adding, refactoring, fixing, reviewing, designing, or choosing libraries. Also trigger on ponytail, be lazy, simplest solution, minimal solution, YAGNI, do less, shortest path, over-engineering, bloat, boilerplate, or unnecessary dependencies. Do NOT use for non-coding requests such as general knowledge, prose, translation, summaries, or recipes.

skills.name: ponytail-audit
skills.description: Whole-repo audit for over-engineering. Scans the entire codebase instead of a diff and reports what to delete, simplify, or replace with standard library or native equivalents. Trigger on audit this codebase, audit for over-engineering, what can I delete from this repo, find bloat, or ponytail-audit.

skills.name: ponytail-debt
skills.description: Harvest every ponytail comment in the codebase into a debt ledger so deliberate shortcuts and deferrals are tracked. Trigger on ponytail debt, what did ponytail defer, list the shortcuts, ponytail ledger, or what was marked for later.

skills.name: ponytail-gain
skills.description: Show ponytail's measured impact as a compact scoreboard: less code, less cost, and more speed from benchmark medians. Trigger on ponytail gain, what does ponytail save, show ponytail impact, or ponytail scoreboard.

skills.name: ponytail-help
skills.description: Quick-reference card for all ponytail modes, skills, and commands. Trigger on ponytail help, what ponytail commands, or how do I use ponytail.

skills.name: ponytail-review
skills.description: Code review focused exclusively on over-engineering. Finds reinvented standard library, unneeded dependencies, speculative abstractions, and dead flexibility. Trigger on review for over-engineering, what can we delete, is this over-engineered, simplify review, or ponytail-review.

skills.name: pptx
skills.description: Use any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading or extracting text; editing existing presentations; combining slides; or working with templates, layouts, speaker notes, and comments. Trigger on deck, slides, presentation, PowerPoint, .pptx, or .potx.

skills.name: show-me
skills.description: Help the user understand the current topic visually with concise diagrams, code-shape sketches, and focused HTML artifacts.
